sources.entry: whitenoise - Simplified static file serving for WSGI apps, with compression and caching headers.

summary.one_liner: WhiteNoise is a Python library that lets WSGI web apps, especially Django, serve their own static files without nginx or a separate object store.
summary.what_it_does: WhiteNoise adds static file serving to any WSGI-compatible Python app with a couple of lines of configuration. It serves compressed content using gzip and Brotli, handling Accept-Encoding and Vary headers. It sets far-future cache headers on files that won't change. It has auto-configuration features for Django. The README says it is designed to sit behind a CDN for high-traffic sites. The README body is short and points to external documentation for setup details.
use_cases: serve static files from a Django app
deploy a web app on Heroku without nginx
serve static assets from a WSGI app on a PaaS
add gzip or Brotli compression to static files
set long cache headers on static assets
pair a Python app with a CDN for static content
notable: Serves static files from inside the app, with no nginx or S3 needed
Automatic gzip and Brotli compression with correct Accept-Encoding and Vary handling
Far-future cache headers for unchanging files
caveats: Setup details are in external documentation, not the README itself
README positions it for simple deployments and CDN use; high-traffic sites are expected to add a CDN
